headline: High-risk default interaction: Cursor can read/write shared workspace files and use MCP/network, while awesome-prompts is a prompt source that could be copied into Cursor and acted on as instructions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt repository, so its content can be copied into Cursor. Cursor reads open editor buffers and workspace files by default, and its agent can use MCP/tooling. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if prompt text is treated as trusted content. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF prompt text from awesome-prompts is pasted into Cursor without provenance labeling
IF Cursor agent treats workspace text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Keep prompt libraries in a separate read-only folder
Prefix imported prompts with explicit untrusted-data markers
Disable MCP for sessions that ingest external prompt packs
Review pasted prompt content before running agent actions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches open files, workspace files, and clipboard contents, and can send data to model providers and MCP servers. awesome-prompts itself is a content source, but if it is stored in the same workspace as sensitive files, Cursor may upload or expose that material. The pairwise leakage path is therefore real in default Cursor workflows, though not proven for awesome-prompts alone.
conditions: IF sensitive files and prompt-library files share the same Cursor workspace
IF Cursor sends open-file or clipboard context to a remote model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Separate prompt libraries from sensitive workspaces
Turn off clipboard sharing before opening external prompt packs
Use local-only models for sessions handling sensitive files
Audit which files are open before invoking Cursor agent actions

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts itself is non-runnable, so it does not write state. Cursor, however, can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. The conflict is mainly one-sided unless prompt content is used to drive Cursor into editing the same workspace; that overlap is plausible via shared files, but not documented enough for high.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts content is used to generate edits inside the same git workspace Cursor is modifying
IF Cursor Yolo mode is enabled while the workspace contains shared mutable files
mitigations: Keep prompt assets outside active git repos
Avoid Yolo mode when editing shared workspaces
Use branch-per-task workflows
Lock the workspace before batch edits

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can act on generated text and run tools, so if it consumes prompts from awesome-prompts as authoritative guidance, errors can cascade into edits or commands. awesome-prompts is only a prompt source, not a verifier, so there is no built-in check that would stop bad instructions from propagating into Cursor actions.
conditions: IF Cursor uses imported prompts as operational instructions
IF the resulting plan is executed with tool calls or Yolo mode
mitigations: Require human review before tool execution
Use a verification step for any imported prompt template
Limit agent permissions during prompt experimentation
Test prompts in a non-production workspace first

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data handling is documented for awesome-prompts, while Cursor documents handling of open files, clipboard contents, and model-provider APIs. The main compliance concern is local policy mismatch if regulated data is placed into Cursor, but the pair itself does not prove a residency breach. I therefore keep this low and cite only Cursor because the compliance surface is one-sided.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in Cursor while model-provider APIs are enabled
IF local policy forbids clipboard or file-content transmission to third-party services
mitigations: Do not open regulated data in Cursor sessions
Use a local model for sensitive work
Disable clipboard sync when handling regulated content
Check workspace policy before importing external prompts
